Config.description:
Named quake windows. The built-in default profile remains available when
omitted. Profile references and display identifiers are resolved at
runtime.

watch_config.description:
Reload the configuration file automatically when it, or a theme file
it uses, changes on disk.

LinkModifiers.description: Modifiers joined with hyphens, without duplicates. Defaults to cmd on macOS and ctrl on Linux. macOS rejects ctrl; this platform restriction is checked at runtime.

NewTabDirectory.description: Working-directory policy for newly opened tabs.

oneOf.description: Use a usable local directory reported by the active terminal.
Always use Huterm's platform launch default.

placement.description: Where the palette sits within the window: `top` or `center`.

retain_query.description:
Keep the search text after the palette is cancelled, so reopening
within `retain_query_seconds` restores it selected.

retain_query_seconds.description: How long a cancelled palette's search text is retained, 0 to 3600.

PalettePlacement.description: Where the command palette sits within its window.

oneOf.description: Anchored near the top edge of the window.

Centred on the window at the palette's full height, so filtering
results never moves the input line.
Each window zooms panes on its own.

The tab owns the zoom: every window set to `shared` shows the same
zoomed pane, and windows set to `view` ignore it.

layout_cycle.description:
The layouts `next_pane_layout` and `previous_pane_layout` step
through, in order: built-in names (`columns`, `rows`, `main_left`,
`main_top`, and `tiled`) or names from `[panes.layouts]`.

additionalProperties.description: A layout template, such as `columns(pane 60%, rows(*))`.

layouts.description:
Named pane layouts, each a layout template: `columns(...)` places
its children left to right and `rows(...)` top to bottom; `pane`
takes one pane, `*` shares the remaining panes, and `grid(*)` tiles
them; a child may end with a share such as `60%`. For example,
`columns(pane 60%, rows(*))`. Names are lowercase letters, digits,
and underscores, starting with a letter, and may not be a built-in
layout's name.

zoom.description: Who owns a pane's zoom: `view` or `shared`.

animation.description:
How the window shows and hides. Auto fades fullscreen windows and
fades and slides others from their side.

animation_ms.description: Animation duration in milliseconds, from 0 to 1000.

display.description:
The display the window opens on: the active one, the one under the
pointer, the primary one, or `id:` and a platform display
identifier. Display availability is checked at runtime.

fullscreen.description: Covers the whole display frame instead of a part of its work area.

height.description:
Fraction of the display work area, greater than zero and at most
one. Fullscreen uses the full display frame.

hide_on_focus_loss.description: Hides the window when another application takes focus.

position.description:
The display edge the window sits against. Center centers it on both
axes. A fullscreen window uses it only as the edge Slide animates
from.

width.description:
Fraction of the display work area, greater than zero and at most
one. Fullscreen uses the full display frame.

family.description: Font family. Defaults to Menlo on macOS and monospace on Linux.

clipboard_write.description:
Allow or deny system clipboard writes requested by terminal content.
Reload applies to existing terminals; explicit Copy and Paste commands
are unaffected.

close_on_exit.x-huterm-label: Close a pane when its shell exits

engine.description:
Deprecated compatibility setting. Both legacy values use Ghostty;
remove this field.

new_tab_directory.x-huterm-label: New tabs and panes start in

right_click.description:
What a right-click on the terminal does: open the context menu,
paste, copy the selection or else paste, or nothing. While an
application takes the mouse, Shift+right-click applies it.

scrollback_bytes.description:
Optional size limit on each terminal's screen and history: a byte count,
or digits and a unit such as "64MiB" or "50MB" (B, KB, MB, GB in powers
of 1000; KiB, MiB, GiB in powers of 1024; units ignore case, so b also
means bytes), at most 16GiB. 0 keeps no history. Whichever of it and
`scrollback_rows` is reached first applies. Ghostty frees history a page
at a time and always allows the visible screen rounded up to whole pages
plus one more, so a tiny value keeps up to about two pages. Reload
applies it to open terminals.

scrollback_compression.description:
Compress each terminal's history once it has been idle for a quarter
of a second. Text-heavy history shrinks to about a tenth of its memory
and reads back exactly as before. The first width change after
compression takes two to three times longer, because it restores all
history. Reload applies it to open terminals; turning it off leaves
history already compressed until something reads it.

scrollback_rows.description:
Live history each terminal keeps above its screen, in screen rows: a
line that wraps counts once for each row it fills. 0 keeps none,
whatever `scrollback_bytes` says. The oldest history is freed a page
at a time, about 570 rows at 80 columns, so a terminal can hold up to
a page fewer, and a smaller nonzero limit keeps up to one page. It
counts rows; `scrollback_bytes` limits size. Reload applies it to open
terminals; lowering it discards the oldest rows at once.

term.description: Terminal identity for newly spawned shells.

oneOf.description:
Admit one snapshot per delivered display frame, plus at most one extra
snapshot for pending viewport changes.
Admit another dirty snapshot as soon as its predecessor completes.

RightClickAction.description:
What a right-click on the terminal does when no application has taken
the mouse, or with Shift held when one has.

oneOf.description: Open the terminal's context menu at the pointer.
Paste the clipboard.
Copy and clear the selection, or paste when nothing is selected.
Do nothing.

name.description: Bundled, inline, or adjacent theme name. Existence is checked at runtime.

oneOf.description: Only while the pointer is over the tab.
On the active tab, and on any hovered tab.
On every tab.

TabDirectory.description: How tab labels show a directory. The local home directory is always `~`.

oneOf.description: The last path component, such as `huterm`.

The full path, relative to home when under it, such as
`~/Projects/huterm`.

The path with parent components shortened to their first character,
such as `~/P/huterm`.

TabLabel.description:
Metadata used to resolve automatic tab labels. A custom tab name always
wins; each mode falls back to the terminal title, then the launched
program.

oneOf.description:
A running program's own title, else its name; at an idle shell, the
directory.
The title set by the shell or program.
The foreground program's name.
The current directory.
The foreground program's name and the current directory.

TabNotch.description:
Where a top tab bar goes on a notched display in non-native fullscreen:
below the notch across the window, or beside the camera housing on one
side, giving that height back to the terminal.

oneOf.description:
Tabs share the window's title-bar row. Where no title bar exists
(fullscreen, Quake windows, or a window manager drawing the title
bar) the tabs take a top bar instead.

always_show.x-huterm-label: Show the tab bar with one tab

close_button.description: When a tab shows its close button; hovering a tab always shows it.

notch.description: Put a top bar beside a display notch in non-native fullscreen.

pill_accent.description: Draws the accent bar inside the active pill; ignored by other styles.
pill_accent.x-huterm-label: Accent bar in the active pill

position.description:
Where tabs sit: top, bottom, left, right, or titlebar. Defaults to
titlebar on macOS and top on Linux.

TerminalIdentity.description: Terminal identity advertised to local applications.

oneOf.description: Use `xterm-huterm` when its terminfo entry is available.
Advertise Huterm's private terminfo entry.
Use the widely installed compatibility entry.

UpdateConfig.description:
Optional overrides for the platform updater.

Leaving either field unset preserves the updater's stored preference. On a
fresh macOS profile, Sparkle asks about automatic checks on the second
launch and uses a 24-hour interval.

automatic_checks.description:
Enable or disable scheduled update checks without Sparkle's consent
prompt. Omit to preserve Sparkle's stored choice; a fresh macOS
profile asks on its second launch.

check_interval_hours.description:
Scheduled update-check interval in whole hours. Omit to preserve
Sparkle's stored interval; a fresh profile uses 24 hours.

macos_native_menus.description:
Open the window, tab, pane, and terminal menus as native macOS
menus. Off draws them in Huterm's own style, as Linux always does.

menu_button.description:
Show the window menu button in the title bar, or in the tab bar
when the window has no title bar. Every item stays reachable through
shortcuts or the command palette.

shortcut_hints.description:
Show key hints on the scroll pill and on dialog and panel buttons.
The command palette and menus always show their shortcuts.
